collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 5-13)

collection.description: After a storm the tide line is thick with things that do not belong to the sea: gather it all up, or let the child keep treasures.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: After last night's storm, the tide line is thick with seaweed, driftwood and things that don't belong to the sea: bright scraps of plastic, a sandal far too small for anyone on Isola, a lid with no pot, a long tangle of colored rope. (friend) is running along the beach with (friend.his/her) arms full of treasure. (subject) is looking at the whole long line of it, frowning.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) is allowed to keep three things. (friend.He/she) chooses the tiny sandal, a red lid, and a piece of something hard and green that the sea has worn smooth. (friend.He/she) lines them up outside (friend.his/her) hut like a museum. Grown-ups come to look. Everybody has a theory about where they came from. Nobody's theory matches anybody else's.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) gets a basket, and then several more, and soon half the village is out on the sand. The good rope is kept. The odd lids become scoops. The rest goes in a pit far up the beach, away from the water. By evening the sand is clean. Three days later, after a smaller storm, there is more. (subject) sighs. Nobody knows where it all comes from. It just keeps coming.
